file_types: node + link with date field
description: Launch uploaded node and distance-link data, switch into Epi Curve, and select Date of symptom onset Date.
primary_assertions: Epi Curve opens; the uploaded symptom-onset field can be selected; rendered SVG bars appear; axis labels render on the uploaded-data path.
notes: This is the maintained uploaded-data Epi smoke baseline for the COVID symptom-onset fixture.

file_types: node with sequences and date field
description: Launch a sequence node list that can derive links, switch into Epi Curve, and select Diagnosis date.
primary_assertions: Epi Curve opens; diagnosis-date bars render from uploaded sequence-node metadata; the uploaded path works without a separate link file.
notes: This covers the sequence-derived node-list launch path for Epi Curve.

file_types: matrix + node metadata
description: Launch an uploaded distance matrix merged with uploaded node metadata, switch into Epi Curve, and select Diagnosis date.
primary_assertions: Diagnosis-date bars render after matrix launch; the node metadata merge survives into Epi Curve; uploaded matrix coverage is no longer 2D-only.
notes: This gives Epi Curve a maintained matrix-backed load path without needing a separate dedicated fixture family.

file_types: fasta + node metadata
description: Launch uploaded FASTA merged with uploaded node metadata, switch into Epi Curve, and select Diagnosis date.
primary_assertions: Diagnosis-date bars render after FASTA launch; the node metadata merge survives into Epi Curve; uploaded FASTA coverage is no longer 2D-only.
notes: This gives Epi Curve a maintained FASTA-backed load path without introducing a new synthetic fixture.

file_types: sequence node + epi link
description: Launch uploaded mixed-origin node + epi-link data, switch into Epi Curve, and select Diagnosis date.
primary_assertions: Diagnosis-date bars render on the mixed-origin launch path; the view remains usable when link origins are mixed.
notes: This keeps the mixed-origin upload path represented in the maintained Epi suite.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Open the uploaded Epi Curve export dialog and write a PNG file to downloads.
primary_assertions: The export dialog opens; writing a non-empty PNG file into cypress/downloads succeeds on uploaded data.
notes: This is the maintained uploaded-data PNG export baseline for Epi Curve.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Open the uploaded Epi Curve export dialog and write an SVG file to downloads.
primary_assertions: The export dialog opens; writing an SVG file containing `<svg` into cypress/downloads succeeds on uploaded data.
notes: This is the maintained uploaded-data SVG export baseline for Epi Curve.

file_types: sample dataset
description: Exercise single-date Epi settings such as bin size, cumulative mode, legend positioning, and label sizing.
primary_assertions: The sample-data Epi spec covers SVG bar updates, axis label sizing, legend visibility and placement, and cumulative versus noncumulative transitions.
notes: Useful view-mechanics coverage exists, but it is still sample-data-only.

file_types: sample dataset
description: Color Epi Curve by Cluster or Node Color on sample data and verify the bars react to filtering and global styling changes.
primary_assertions: The sample-data spec covers cluster-color recompute after threshold changes and the Node Color path after global node-color edits.
notes: This is a high-value uploaded-data migration target, but it is not yet in the maintained journeys suite.

file_types: sample dataset
description: Exercise the multi-date Epi graph types with independent date fields and colors.
primary_assertions: The sample-data spec covers side-by-side and overlay graph types, per-field colors, legend placement, and cumulative toggling.
notes: This remains sample-data-only until a stable uploaded-data migration is added.

subarea: Direct file launch to Epi Curve default view
file_types: node + link with date field
description: Set File Settings default view to Epi Curve before launch and confirm the uploaded dataset lands directly in Epi Curve.
primary_assertions: The Processing Files flow clears and the uploaded dataset reaches an interactive Epi Curve without needing a post-launch view switch.
notes: File Settings now exposes `Epi Curve` as a launch option and Epi launch now marks itself rendered so the shared processing modal clears on direct launch.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Migrate the single-date Epi settings coverage off the sample dataset onto uploaded data.
primary_assertions: Bin Size, cumulative mode, legend position, label size, and legend size update the rendered uploaded-data SVG and stored widget values without reopening the view.
notes: Promoted into the maintained uploaded-data controls journey on the COVID node+link fixture.

subarea: X-axis Interval control on uploaded data
file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Change X-axis Interval on uploaded data and verify tick density or labels update, including the bin-size-specific control visibility.
primary_assertions: When Bin Size is not Year the X-axis Interval control is visible; changing it updates the rendered x-axis ticks; switching Bin Size to Year hides the control and Quarter resets the interval safely.
notes: Maintained uploaded-data coverage now exercises configureXAxisSettings() through the live Epi controls.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Color the uploaded Epi Curve by Cluster, then change filtering threshold and verify legend categories and bar fills recompute.
primary_assertions: Cluster count changes refresh the rendered legend and bar color set automatically through clusterUpdate$; stale cluster colors do not remain after the threshold move.
notes: Promoted from the sample-data-only spec into a maintained uploaded-data styling journey.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Color the uploaded Epi Curve by Node Color, then change global node-color mappings and verify the bar fills update.
primary_assertions: Switching node-color variable or editing a category color in Global Settings immediately changes the rendered uploaded-data Epi fills; resetting to a fixed node color collapses back to one fill.
notes: Promoted from the sample-data-only spec into a maintained uploaded-data styling journey.

file_types: uploaded node + link with at least 3 date fields
description: Launch uploaded data into Epi Curve, switch to Multi: Side by Side, populate Date Field 1-3, and verify the view renders all configured series.
primary_assertions: Additional date selectors appear; each selected field maps to a rendered series or legend entry; uploaded data renders multiple date series on the maintained node+link fixture.
notes: Covered with the existing COVID uploaded fixture because it already contains Collection Date, symptom-onset, and symptoms-resolved fields.

file_types: uploaded node + link with at least 3 date fields
description: Switch the uploaded Epi Curve multi-date graph type from Side by Side to Overlay and verify colors and geometry update correctly.
primary_assertions: The graph-type widget changes to Multi: Overlay; per-field colors stay mapped to the correct series; overlay rendering remains visually distinct from side-by-side on uploaded data.
notes: Covered in the maintained uploaded-data controls journey by comparing side-by-side and overlay geometry and opacity.

subarea: Uploaded multi-date legend and cumulative controls
file_types: uploaded node + link with at least 3 date fields
description: While on uploaded multi-date data, exercise legend placement and cumulative toggling to confirm the multi-series control paths remain live outside the sample dataset.
primary_assertions: Legend position changes move the multi-date legend and cumulative mode changes the rendered bar progression for all active date series.
notes: Promoted from the sample-data-only spec into the maintained uploaded-data controls journey.

subarea: PNG advanced scale and calculated resolution
file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Open PNG export advanced settings, change Scale, and verify the calculated resolution updates before export.
primary_assertions: The advanced accordion opens; changing Scale updates the Resolution text; exporting after the change still writes a non-empty PNG artifact.
notes: The maintained export suite now covers both the default PNG/SVG paths and the advanced PNG scale-resolution path.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Verify the advanced PNG export dialog does not expose an unsupported quality control.
primary_assertions: The advanced export accordion omits the inert PNG quality slider, so the dialog no longer advertises a control the export path cannot honor.
notes: Resolved by removing the unsupported `network-export-quality` control from the Epi export dialog and asserting its absence in the maintained export spec.

subarea: Uploaded single-date fixed Epi color and Color By visibility
file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Keep Epi Curve in single-date mode, set a fixed bar color, then switch Color By away from and back to None.
primary_assertions: When Color By is None the single-date color picker is visible and changing it collapses all bar fills to the configured fixed color; switching Color By to Cluster hides that picker and replaces the fixed fill path with categorical colors.
notes: This covers the primary `epiCurve-colors[0]` control path that was not represented in the original tracker.

file_types: uploaded node + link with date field
description: Reset active single-date and multi-date Epi date fields to None and verify the chart clears instead of leaving stale SVG output.
primary_assertions: Clearing the active date selection empties rendered bars and axes in single-date mode, and clearing all selected fields does the same in multi-date mode while the stored widget values end at ['None','None','None'].
notes: Added after auditing the component uncovered an untracked stale-SVG risk in the early-return refresh paths.
